q: Success depends ___ hard work.
She is married ___ a lawyer.
I'm thinking ___ changing my job.
The course consists ___ ten modules.
He is very good ___ mathematics.
We arrived ___ the airport two hours early.
e: arrive at a building or point; never 'arrive to'.

q: Many people are worried ___ climate change.
I'm interested ___ studying abroad. (one preposition)
She dreams ___ becoming a surgeon. (one preposition)
My results are the same ___ last year. (one word)
e: the same as, not 'the same than / that'.

q: This city is very different ___ my home town. (one preposition)
e: different from (also 'different to' in British English).

q: The new law resulted ___ higher prices for consumers. (one preposition)
He insisted ___ paying for dinner. (one preposition)
It depends of the weather tomorrow.
fix: It depends on the weather tomorrow.

q: She is responsible of the marketing department.
fix: She is responsible for the marketing department.

q: We need to discuss about the new project.
fix: We need to discuss the new project.

q: I am agree with your opinion.
I have been waiting you for an hour.
a: I have been waiting for you for an hour.

q: She explained me the problem.
a: She explained the problem to me.

q: I look forward to hear from you.
a: I look forward to hearing from you.
e: 'To' is a preposition here, so the verb takes -ing.
